q: 1. Venturimeter is used to
options: measure the velocity of a flowing liquid
measure the pressure of a flowing liquid
measure the discharge of liquid flowing in a pipe
measure the pressure difference of liquid flowing between two points
explain: A venturimeter is a standard device used to calculate the volume flow rate (discharge) in a pipeline.

q: 2. The length of the divergent cone in a venturimeter is _________ that of the convergent cone.
explain: The divergent cone is longer (angle of 5-7°) to prevent flow separation and minimize energy loss.

q: 3. The velocity of the liquid flowing through the divergent portion of a venturimeter
explain: As the cross-sectional area increases in the divergent part, the velocity must decrease per the continuity equation.

q: 4. The divergent portion of a venturimeter is made longer than convergent portion in order to
options: avoid the tendency of breaking away the stream of liquid
explain: A gradual expansion (longer length) ensures the flow stays attached to the walls, preventing turbulence and boundary layer separation.

q: 5. In order to measure the flow with a venturimeter, it is installed in
options: any direction and in any location
explain: A venturimeter works accurately in any orientation as long as the Bernoulli equation accounts for the change in elevation (Z).

q: 6. Coefficient of resistance is the ratio of
options: area at vena contracta to area of orifice
loss of head in the orifice to the head available at exit
explain: Coefficient of resistance (Cr) relates the energy loss due to friction to the available kinetic head.

q: 7. A jet of water discharging from a 40 mm diameter orifice has a diameter of 32 mm at its vena contracta. The coefficient of contraction is
explain: Cc = Area of jet / Area of orifice = (32/40)² = 0.8² = 0.64.

q: 8. Coefficient of velocity is defined as the ratio of
options: actual velocity of jet at vena contracta to the theoretical velocity
area of jet at vena contracta to the area of orifice
actual discharge through an orifice to the theoretical discharge
explain: Cv = Actual Velocity / Theoretical Velocity. It accounts for losses due to friction.

q: 9. The theoretical velocity of jet at vena contracta is
explain: Derived from Bernoulli's equation (v = √2gh), assuming no losses.

q: 10. Coefficient of discharge Cd is equal to
explain: The overall discharge coefficient is the product of the contraction and velocity coefficients.

q: 11. An average value of coefficient of velocity is
explain: For a standard sharp-edged orifice, Cv typically ranges from 0.95 to 0.99.

q: 12. The coefficient of velocity is determined experimentally by using the relation
explain: Using the trajectory of the jet, where x is horizontal distance and y is vertical drop, this formula solves for actual velocity.

q: 13. An orifice is said to be large, if
options: the size of orifice is large
the velocity of flow is large
the available head is more than 5 times the height of orifice
the available head is less than 5 times the height of orifice
explain: If head H < 5d, the pressure variation across the orifice is significant, and it is classified as a 'large orifice'.

q: 14. A pipe of length more than double the diameter of orifice fitted externally or internally to the orifice is called a
explain: A mouthpiece is a short tube used to increase the discharge through an orifice.

q: 15. In a short cylindrical external mouthpiece, the vena contracta occurs at a distance _________ the diameter of the orifice from the outlet of orifice.
explain: For an external mouthpiece, the jet contracts to its minimum area at approximately 0.25d from the inlet.

q: 16. The discharge through an external mouth piece is given by
explain: The average Cd for an external mouthpiece is 0.855, significantly higher than a simple orifice (0.62).

q: 17. The coefficient of discharge for an external mouthpiece depends upon
explain: The length relative to diameter determines whether the mouthpiece runs full, affecting the Cd.

q: 18. In an internal mouthpiece, if the jet after contraction does not touch the sides of the mouthpiece, then the mouthpiece is said to be
explain: When the jet discharges without wetting the internal walls, it is in a 'running free' condition.

q: 19. The coefficient of discharge for an external mouthpiece is
explain: For an external cylindrical mouthpiece, the coefficient of discharge ($C_d$) is approximately 0.855, which is higher than a sharp-edged orifice due to the reduction in contraction.

q: 20. An internal mouthpiece is said to be running free if the length of the mouthpiece is ............ the diameter of the orifice.
explain: In a Borda's mouthpiece (internal), if the length is less than twice the diameter, the jet of liquid does not touch the sides, and it is said to be 'running free'.

q: 21. When an internal mouthpiece is running free, the discharge through the mouthpiece is ............
explain: For an internal mouthpiece running free, the theoretical coefficient of discharge is 0.5. Therefore, $Q = 0.5a\sqrt{2gH}$.

q: 22. The discharge through a convergent mouthpiece is ............ the discharge through an internal mouthpiece of the same diameter and head of water.
explain: A convergent mouthpiece has a $C_d$ near 1.0, while a Borda's mouthpiece running free has a $C_d$ of 0.5. Thus, the discharge through the convergent one is roughly double.

q: 23. A notch is used to measure ............ of liquids.
explain: Notches and weirs are standard hydraulic structures used to measure the rate of flow (discharge) of liquids in open channels.

q: 24. The discharge over a rectangular notch is ............
explain: The standard formula for discharge over a rectangular notch is $Q = \frac{2}{3} C_d \cdot b \sqrt{2g} \cdot H^{3/2}$.

q: 25. The discharge over a right angled notch is ............
explain: For a V-notch (triangular notch), the discharge formula is $Q = \frac{8}{15} C_d \tan(\theta/2) \sqrt{2g} \cdot H^{5/2}$. For a right-angled notch, $\theta = 90°$, so $	an(45°) = 1$.

q: 26. If the coefficient of discharge is 0.6, then the discharge over a right angled notch is ............
explain: Plugging $C_d = 0.6$ into the V-notch formula $Q = \frac{8}{15} \times 0.6 	imes \sqrt{2 	imes 9.81} 	imes H^{5/2}$ results in approximately $1.417 H^{5/2}$.

q: 27. The discharge over a rectangular notch is ............
explain: Based on the formula $Q =  rac{2}{3} C_d b \sqrt{2g} H^{3/2}$, discharge is directly proportional to the head raised to the power of 1.5.

q: 28. The discharge over a triangular notch is ............
explain: Based on the formula $Q =  rac{8}{15} C_d 	an(	heta/2) \sqrt{2g} H^{5/2}$, discharge is directly proportional to $H^{2.5}$.

q: 29. The error in discharge (dQ/Q) to the error in measurement of head (dH/H) over a rectangular notch is given by ............
explain: By differentiating $Q = kH^{3/2}$, we get $dQ/Q = 1.5 (dH/H)$.

q: 30. The error in discharge (dQ/Q) to the error in measurement of head (dH/H) over a triangular notch is given by ............
explain: By differentiating $Q = kH^{5/2}$, we get $dQ/Q = 2.5 (dH/H)$.

q: 31. An error of 1% in measuring head over the crest of the notch (H) will produce an error of ............ in discharge over a rectangular notch.
explain: Using $dQ/Q = 1.5 (dH/H)$, a 1% error in head results in $1.5 	imes 1\% = 1.5\%$ error in discharge.

q: 32. An error of 1% in measuring head over the apex of the notch (H) will produce an error of ............ in discharge over a triangular notch.
explain: Using $dQ/Q = 2.5 (dH/H)$, a 1% error in head results in $2.5 	imes 1\% = 2.5\%$ error in discharge.

q: 33. A structure used to dam up a stream or river over which the water flows is called ............
explain: While a dam holds water, a 'weir' is specifically the structure built across a river over which water flows for measurement or regulation.

q: 34. The sheet of water flowing over a notch or a weir is known as ............
explain: The continuous sheet of water that overflows the weir or notch is technically called the 'nappe' or 'vein'.

q: 35. The top of the weir over which the water flows is known as ............
explain: The top edge or surface of a weir or notch over which the water flows is called the 'crest' or 'sill'.

q: 36. According to Francis formula, the discharge over a rectangular weir is ............
explain: Francis formula accounts for end contractions: $Q =  rac{2}{3} C_d (L - 0.1nH) \sqrt{2g} H^{3/2}$, where $n$ is the number of end contractions.

q: 37. When the coefficient of discharge (Cd) is 0.623, then the general equation for discharge over a rectangular weir is ............
explain: Substituting $C_d = 0.623$ and $g = 9.81$ into the Francis formula $ rac{2}{3} C_d \sqrt{2g}$ yields the constant 1.84.

q: 38. The Cippoletti is a ............ weir.
explain: A Cippoletti weir is a trapezoidal weir with a side slope of 1 horizontal to 4 vertical (1:4).

q: 39. The Francis formula for the discharge over Cippoletti weir is ............
explain: The Cippoletti weir is designed to compensate for end contractions, simplifying the formula to $Q = 1.84 LH^{3/2}$.

q: 40. In a broad-crested weir, the discharge is maximum if the head of water on the downstream side of weir is ............ the head of water on the upstream side of weir.
explain: For maximum discharge over a broad-crested weir, the depth of water over the crest ($h$) should be $ rac{2}{3} H$.

q: 41. The maximum discharge over a broad crested weir is ............
explain: The maximum discharge is $Q_{max} = 1.71 C_d L H^{3/2}$, derived using the critical depth condition.

q: 42. A weir, generally, used as a spillway of a dam is ............
explain: An Ogee weir is shaped to follow the profile of the lower nappe of a ventilated jet, making it the most efficient and common shape for dam spillways.

q: 43. When the water level on the downstream side of a weir is above the top surface of a weir, the weir is known as ............
explain: A weir is considered submerged or drowned when the water level on the downstream side is higher than the crest of the weir.

q: 44. In a free nappe ............
options: the pressure below the nappe is atmospheric
the pressure below the nappe is negative
the pressure above the nappe is atmospheric
the pressure above the nappe is negative
explain: For a nappe to be 'free', air must circulate freely underneath it, maintaining atmospheric pressure below the water sheet.

q: 45. In a depressed nappe ............
options: the pressure below the nappe is atmospheric
the pressure below the nappe is negative
the pressure above the nappe is atmospheric
the pressure above the nappe is negative
explain: In a depressed nappe, air is trapped and partially exhausted by the flowing water, creating a partial vacuum (negative pressure) underneath.

q: 46. The discharge through a siphon spillway is ............
explain: A siphon spillway acts like a large submerged orifice or pipe under a head $H$, where $H$ is the difference between upstream and downstream water levels.

q: 47. According to Chezy's formula, the discharge through an open channel is ............
explain: Chezy's formula for velocity is $v = C\sqrt{mi}$. Discharge $Q = Av$, so $Q = AC\sqrt{mi}$.

q: 48. According to Manning's formula, the discharge through an open channel is ............
explain: Manning's formula for velocity is $v = M \cdot m^{2/3} \cdot i^{1/2}$. Therefore, $Q = A \cdot M \cdot m^{2/3} \cdot i^{1/2}$.

q: 49. The discharge through a channel of rectangular section will be maximum, if ............
options: its depth is twice the breadth
its breadth is twice the depth
its depth is thrice the breadth
its breadth is thrice the depth
explain: For a rectangular channel to be most economical, the hydraulic radius should be half the depth ($R = y/2$), which occurs when the width $b$ is twice the depth $y$ ($b = 2y$).

q: 50. The discharge through a channel of trapezoidal section is maximum when ............
options: width of channel at the top is equal to twice the width at the bottom
depth of channel is equal to the width at the bottom
the sloping side is equal to half the width at the top
the sloping side is equal to the width at the bottom
explain: A trapezoidal section is most economical when the length of the sloping side is equal to half of the top width.
